_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Contra (ADR-0184, amended 2026-09-14: 'a
navigation cheat is a third pass, and it feeds every surface').
This file is data. A second game is a second file beside this one - no code
change - as long as its navigation address is read off a published RAM map
or the vendored cheat database (ADR-0184 s5: no code is invented).

navigation.label: current level
navigation.source: DataCrystal, Contra (NES) RAM map: $0030 holds the current level, 0x00-0x07 = stages 1-8, 0x09 = game over. Published map, cited per ADR-0184 s5.

_defaultsComment: The entry script types the Konami code at the title screen (30 lives).
ADR-0184 s3 ranks that first and it is not a cheat at all: it writes the
game's own variable through the game's own routine. Measured 2026-09-14:
the plain mint (3 lives) reaches GAME OVER inside 40 s on stages 1 and 4,
so a blind warp with 3 lives records the game-over screen and little else.
The body is repeated by record_navigation_sweep.py until it covers the
whole run: ADR-0184's measurement found stage1-run.txt leaves 82% of a
300 s recording with nothing pressed, and effective input time is what
moved the panorama, not the cheat.
_roomsComment: $0030 selects a *level*, not a room inside one: pinned for the run the game
loads the start of that stage and never observes the stage advancing, so a
boss room is unreachable by any value of it (the map declares 0x00-0x07 and
0x09 = game over, and nothing else). A boss is therefore its own session,
entered from the save state that is already in its room and played by the
input script minted beside it (F9.22, scripts/stages/README.md). Those
sessions carry no cheat at all, so they are ADR-0184 s2 'clean' passes and
every surface may read them for that reason instead.
The three states are unversioned (a CHR RAM state carries the game's art).
Pass --states <dir> pointing at the folder that holds them; a room whose
state is missing is skipped with a line saying so, never silently.
